arms.better: tm identified the aliasing defect and its implementation passed the hidden PR tests, but it spent 66 tool calls and about 4.06 million reported input tokens on repeated reads and searches before stopping at the 64-step limit without submitting. A short explicit plan, deduplicated file reads, and a safer recovery path after the step limit would have helped the user understand the status and avoid retrying an already long run; `tm events` also printed only generic subcommand help, and the following live-tail command did not explain that it would keep waiting without `--no-follow`.

OpenCode traced the shared-slice append, explained the minimal defensive copy, and reported both its full test run and diff check accurately. It could improve further by adding a focused regression test during its run rather than relying on the later independently restored hidden PR test, and by reporting machine-readable usage/cost in the final summary.
